lead.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's chief executive, and Congress summons him to testify about the suspected Chinese spy
lead.short: Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, resigned on Thursday as its president, chief executive and a board member, with immediate effect, after reports of two extramarital affairs. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor. Nvidia has lost $550bn in stock market value in five days.

why.text: The company whose chips power the AI boom has lost its founder in a week, and Washington now wants answers about China.

more: Senator Tim Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee on 3 December and warned that the panel could subpoena him. Three House committees have summoned him to a closed-door interview on 1 December. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, under scrutiny over sales of advanced Nvidia chips to China, has also been called before the Senate committee.

Huang remains Nvidia's fourth-largest investor, with about 3.61% of the company. The board says it will consider internal and external candidates; Micron's Sanjay Mehrotra, Palo Alto Networks' Nikesh Arora and Google Cloud's Thomas Kurian are among names in reports. Kress, finance chief since 2013, keeps that role while she leads the company.

update.new: Huang resigned and has been summoned by Congress.
update.front: Nvidia's founder is gone, and Congress wants to hear from him.

seconds.headline: New Zealand bowl India out for 89 to win the fourth ODI by 244 runs, with Rohit, Kohli and Iyer out for ducks
seconds.short: New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Mount Maunganui on Friday, bowling them out for 89 after making 333. Matt Henry took 6 for 27, dismissing Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and stand-in captain Shreyas Iyer without scoring. India lead the five-match series 2-1 before Sunday's last game at the same ground.

why.text: It is a heavy warning a week before the Test series, on pitches with the seam and bounce that undid India's batters.

more: Will Young made 125 from 108 balls to carry New Zealand to 333. India were 69 for eight in the 23rd over: Ruturaj Gaikwad was caught at second slip off Kyle Jamieson for five, and Axar Patel was dropped at point next ball. India played without Shubman Gill and KL Rahul, who have left the one-day squad to prepare for the Tests.

New Zealand's batters had struggled in the first two games, both won by India, and the third was washed out in Hamilton. The fifth ODI is at Mount Maunganui at 07:30 IST on Sunday, and the first Test starts in Wellington on 19 November.

update.new: New Zealand won by 244 runs; India lead 2-1.
update.front: India's heaviest defeat of the tour cuts their series lead to 2-1.

seconds.headline: Retail inflation rises to 6.09% in October, above the RBI's 6% ceiling for the first time in two years
seconds.short: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, crossing the RBI's 6% upper limit for the first time since October 2024, government data released on Thursday showed. Food inflation climbed to 8.94% from 7.74%, led by onion at 116%, garlic at 61%, ginger at 48% and lemon at 47%.

why.text: Prices are rising faster than the RBI allows, and another rate rise in December now looks likely.

more: Inflation has risen for 12 months in a row, helped by an unfavourable base effect, and prices were also 0.5% higher than in September. Headline inflation was below 4% in only five of 36 states and union territories, including Delhi. Axis Bank's Tanay Dalal expects it to stay above 6% until June 2027, citing "the transmission of global shocks".

The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% last month, and economists widely expect another rise at its meeting on 2 to 4 December. The central bank's own forecast puts inflation at an average of 6% for October to December.

seconds.headline: Modi opens the elevated Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, taking Bengaluru's metro past 100 km
seconds.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · THE HINDU · 13 NOV
seconds.short: Narendra Modi inaugurated the elevated stretch of Namma Metro's Pink Line on Friday, six stations from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere built for about ₹3,470 crore, after taking a ride on it. The opening takes Bengaluru's operational metro network past 100 km for the first time. Public services start on Saturday, 14 November.

why.text: It brings the metro to south Bengaluru's Bannerghatta Road, though the underground link to the city centre is still a year away.

more: The line runs along Bannerghatta Road, and the stations are Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIMB, JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere. The underground section, which will connect the central business district to north Bengaluru, is due in 2027, so the stretch offers only minor relief to the city's traffic, The Hindu reported.

Modi also flagged off the Yesvantpur-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express to coastal Karnataka and Goa, stopping at places including Hassan, Mangaluru, Udupi, Gokarna and Karwar; regular runs start on 15 November. The visit includes works worth over ₹15,600 crore. Karnataka says it pays 84% of the metro's costs and the Centre 16%.

update.front: Bengaluru's newest metro line is open, and services start tomorrow.

stories.headline: The Centre bans Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation for five more years under the anti-terror law
stories.short: The Home Ministry on Friday declared Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association under the UAPA for another five years, the third extension of a ban first imposed in 2016. It said that unless curbed, the group would "continue its subversive activities" and "disrupt the secular fabric of the country".

why.text: It keeps the preacher's organisation shut in India as he remains abroad and under investigation.

more: The notification says the foundation would otherwise "re-organise its activists who are still absconding", create communal disharmony, "propagate anti-national sentiments" and support militancy. The ministry acted under Section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, and the ban runs for five years from its publication in the official gazette.

Naik, born in Mumbai, left India after the bombing of a Dhaka cafe on 1 July 2016 and is being investigated by the National Investigation Agency over alleged terror activities. He is accused of spreading hatred between communities through his Peace TV channel and social media, and is banned from Britain and Canada over his speeches.

facts.ban: five more years under the UAPA

briefs.text: The rate fell from 28 to 18 per lakh people between 2015 and 2025, against a 35% global fall, and 94% of drug-susceptible patients are now treated successfully.

stories.headline: Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer to lead the new Democratic Senate majority
stories.short: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said on Thursday he will challenge Chuck Schumer to be Senate majority leader when Democrats take control in January. "In this election, the American people called for change," Van Hollen said. Schumer replied within a minute that he had "the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader".

why.text: It is the first sign that the midterm victory will bring a fight over whether Democrats turn left.

more: "It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," Van Hollen said. Schumer wrote: "I'm proud of what we've accomplished together, 55 seats and counting is an amazing result." The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December, the first contested vote for Democratic leader in decades.

The race pits the progressive Van Hollen against the centrist Schumer, who recruited many of the winning candidates and raised money for them. Some winners, among them Michigan's senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, did not initially have his support. "I'm going to win it," Schumer told the Associated Press last week.

briefs.text: The Sensex fell as much as 610 points early and was down 0.7% at 81,363 at 2pm. Foreign investors have bought about ₹75,300 crore of shares in November, the most in any month since December 2020.

stories.headline: Anthropic's listing draws about six times as many orders as there are shares, Bloomberg reports
stories.short: Anthropic's share sale has drawn about six times as many orders as there are shares available, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The maker of the Claude models aims to raise up to $64.4bn in the listing and $26bn in a private placement at the same time, which together would be the biggest stock market debut ever.

why.text: Demand for Anthropic is holding up in the same week investors fled Nvidia.

more: Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers will be prioritised, and some buyers will get smaller allocations than they expect, the people said. Details, including demand, could still change. Nvidia has agreed to buy about $10bn of shares in the private placement, Anthropic's filings show. Anthropic did not immediately comment.

Index funds could account for about 28% of the shares offered, or roughly $19bn, as big indexes add the stock within 5 to 15 days of listing, the analytics firm Intropic estimates. Only about 6% of Anthropic's shares are being sold. Trading is due to begin on 19 November under the ticker ANT.

facts.demand: about six times the shares on offer

update.new: Orders are about six times the shares on offer.

briefs.text: Warby Parker's three frames start at $395 in the US, and Gentle Monster's six styles at $449 in the US and South Korea. Samsung makes the computing hardware, Google the software.

briefs.headline: Microsoft's outage of Outlook and its workplace apps enters a second day, and the company says it sees no attack
briefs.text: More than 100,000 users reported Outlook problems on DownDetector, and many in India woke on Friday to inaccessible inboxes. Microsoft blamed elevated load on part of its infrastructure across several regions.

briefs.headline: The Euclid space telescope releases its first big batch of data, covering more than a billion objects
briefs.text: The release spans an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons and starts one of the largest 3D maps of the cosmos. The European Space Agency's telescope is built to study dark matter and dark energy.

briefs.headline: Harry Kane becomes England's most-capped men's player in a win over Croatia, and is rated their best on the night
briefs.text: Kane, already England's record scorer, now has more caps than any other men's player. Morgan Rogers scored for England in the Nations League win at Wembley.

stories.headline: Pat Cummins calls Khawaja's sandpaper claims 'complete and utter nonsense', and Warner says he threw Khawaja under the bus
stories.short: Australia captain Pat Cummins on Friday rejected Usman Khawaja's claim that the whole team knew about the use of sandpaper in the 2018 Cape Town Test, calling his allegation of a scheme "complete and utter nonsense". Hours later, David Warner said Cummins had "threw Uzzie under the bus" and that he still backed Khawaja's account.

why.text: An eight-year-old scandal is splitting the team that lived through it, as Australia's home season starts.

more: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100% wrong," Cummins told a news conference at the Sydney Cricket Ground. "I've said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening." He said Khawaja's book accused him and others of being "architects" of the plan.

Speaking on Fox Cricket during Australia's first ODI against England in Perth, Warner said: "I still stick by Uzzie, and what he's written in that book. It is the truth and I really, really support him." He again called Cricket Australia's investigation "botched". Warner was banned for 12 months over the scandal.

update.new: Cummins answers Khawaja, and Warner hits back.

update.new: Scans show a tear; two weeks to re-evaluation.
